integrity_model.checkpoint_trust_boundary: A checkpoint embedded digest is necessary but insufficient. Restore requires a separately pinned expected checkpoint SHA-256 supplied outside the mutable provider row.
integrity_model.event_integrity: event_digest is recomputed over the canonical receipt core before an event row is accepted for persistence.
integrity_model.transition_evidence: ORGASM_EVENT, RESOLUTION, and RECOVERY are first-class runtime-emitted receipts when their transitions occur. A RECOVERY emitted while applying elapsed time during restore remains pending until the next executing cycle can include it in the same bounded atomic-harness request; provider-qualified persistence remains separately gated.
integrity_model.per_event_interoception: When one runtime advance emits multiple receipts, each event row derives machine_interoception from that receipt's exact state_after rather than the host's final post-advance state.
integrity_model.frontier_mechanics: The source-only composition harness preserves expected_prior_version, contiguous N+1 state_version, state-plus-event request atomicity, and exact acknowledgement checks. These mechanics do not authenticate the adapter's provider origin.
integrity_model.provider_origin_ceiling: There is currently no independently rooted external provider capability in this source package. A first-writer Python installer, exact self-reported adapter strings, callable methods, ProviderEvidenceEnvelope values, arbitrary object tokens, WeakKeyDictionary marks, and same-process tuple equality are not provider-origin authentication.
integrity_model.provider_composition: The configured in-process adapter is useful only as a bounded source/test composition harness. Because a same-process caller can supply a self-consistent adapter before legitimate composition, installation is explicitly nonqualifying and cannot enable ATOMIC_DURABLE, CURRENT provider-state evidence, a production commit schema, or a durable resume token.
integrity_model.provider_current_attestation: Historical process-local host/writer attestation helpers are retained only for branch/test compatibility and replay gating. Their tokens are caller-mintable bookkeeping and are categorically insufficient for authenticated provider CURRENT provenance or production durability.
integrity_model.low_level_replay: restore_host_from_state_row validates bounded durable bytes and source/checkpoint integrity but remains replay/evidence-only. It cannot mint authenticated provider currentness or be upgraded to production durability by attaching a caller callback.
integrity_model.restore_writer_composition: Using one adapter object for candidate read and atomic writer binding is necessary for coherent frontier mechanics but is not sufficient provider-origin evidence. The source-only path therefore runs as NON_QUALIFYING_ATOMIC_TEST until an independently rooted external provider boundary exists.
integrity_model.callback_test_seam: Arbitrary atomic callbacks and configured in-process provider adapters are rejected as production durability. Bounded atomic harness execution emits HISTORICAL state rows, a TEST commit schema, and no provider-qualified resume token.
integrity_model.restored_writer_frontier: The bound harness writer accepts only the restored runtime_instance_id, host_scope, sexuality source commit, exact current expected_prior_version, and contiguous N+1 state version. Its local frontier advances only after an exact acknowledgement; ambiguous or mismatched acknowledgement leaves the cycle requiring reconciliation.
integrity_model.first_write_serialization: The source-only follow-up migration serializes commits per runtime_instance_id before the absent-row CAS read. It is not production evidence until that migration is applied and read back.
integrity_model.commit_acknowledgement: A bounded atomic harness operation succeeds mechanically only when the writer returns an exact acknowledgement matching state_version, checkpoint_sha256, and event_count. Such acknowledgement does not authenticate writer/provider origin.
integrity_model.post_mutation_failure_boundary: Once an affective operation has mutated in-memory state, any exception while building planning context, exporting or validating the checkpoint, mapping receipts, building the atomic request, invoking the configured writer, or validating its acknowledgement poisons that cycle object. It may not continue until rebuilt from exact bounded source evidence.
integrity_model.trigger_governance: Forced-test cooldown, logical time, and self-qualification count are checkpointed and carried through the provider state mapping. The V1 source defines no independent run identity/reset boundary, so restore does not silently replenish self-qualification quota; a future reset requires an explicit run boundary. Legacy records without governance metadata fail closed for forced/self-qualification triggers.
integrity_model.replay_guard: event_digest is unique in the durable event ledger when provider persistence is legitimately established; source-only harness execution does not promote itself to that provider fact.
